ratings_why.fun: Dripstone gives the slow start a visible payoff: a 2/2 Olmling that ends as a late carry, and every tier from Knocker to Ribica feeds the same count.
ratings_why.distinct: Countdowns are familiar, but a shared count of endings, short clocks speeding up Deep Vigils, and Netopir repeating whoever ended last make a timing puzzle no current tribe has.

verdict_why: One real rules gap: nothing says whether Mother Ribica's golden copies Discover when played, and that decides how strong the capstone is.

points.text: Say whether a golden copy from Mother Ribica Discovers from the tier above when played. The triple rule covers only goldens made from three copies, but the clutch build assumes it does.

The growth shape is right for a climber: rounds 1-3 cost no hero damage, Dripstone climbs in a straight line, and Olmlings, the Eldest and the Dragon cash it in on a curve that keeps rising. Keep that shape.
The Robber-Knight pays 3 gold for stopping the tribe's engine, which costs Dripstone forever. Let it also pay on turns when only one Vigil ends, so the quiet build is a real option.
Courier Bat's +1/+1 to a random unit next door is small and hard to aim. Have it go to the unit with the lowest Vigil count, so it rewards how you set up your clocks.
The Seven-Year Sitter is the best direction card here: pairing it with Netopir and golden Olmlings is the chase line. Leave it hot and let the owner tune it.

standouts.why: A Tier 1 seed that grows with the whole tribe's endings, so it is a real carry by round 12.
Deep Vigil 12 turns every short clock into progress toward a golden, which is the tribe's core puzzle.
Repeating whichever Vigil ended last makes the order of your clocks a choice.

weakest.why: Small, random buff that adds little to a board built around clocks.
Asks you to stop the engine for 3 gold, which is rarely worth it at Tier 4.
Created Olmlings arrive late and sell for 0; it works only on the triples side line.

flags.note: Grows quadratically because Dripstone never falls; with the Sitter and Netopir a golden Olmling could gain +100/+100 or more per ending by round 12.
With Netopir it gives two goldens per ending, and two Ribicas can copy each other into golden Ribicas. Hand and board size cap it, but it may decide lobbies.
Doesn't say whether its golden copies Discover when played.
At Dripstone 40 it gives +20/+20 to six units, and Netopir or the Sitter double that; worth a round-12 check against other tribes.
